== Biography ==
Benjamin was born about 1835. He was the son of [[Glasgow-2058|John Glasgow]], and was age 20 living at Killycurragh in April 1856.

On 15 April 1856 at 1st Cookstown Presbyterian, Benjamin Glasgow, 20, married Jane Little (full age) of Orritor Craigs, daughter of George Little. Witnessed by Potters.
<ref>Benjamin Glasgow, Jane Little, 1856, Cookstown] at Irish Civil Registration - Marriages Cookstown https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1856/09507/5445820.pdf </ref>

He passed away 8 February 1870 age 34  and is buried at Derryloran Old Cemetery.
<ref>[https://civilrecords.irishgenealogy.ie/churchrecords/details-civil/4719c121822615 Benjamin Glasgow, 1870, Cookstown, 34] at Irish Civil Registration - Deaths</ref><ref>General Record Office Northern Ireland ref: D/1870/99/1009/3/464	Benjamin	Glasgow	8th February 1870	34		Male	Cookstown</ref> 
<ref>{{FindAGrave|248049772}} - photo of headstone.</ref>

== Research Notes ==

=== Marriage details and the Drapersfield namesake ===

The original 15 April 1856 marriage entry records Benjamin as a 20-year-old bachelor merchant resident in Cookstown and his father [[Glasgow-2058|John Glasgow]] as a merchant. [[Little-17969|Jane Little]] was a full-age spinster of Oritor Craigs, daughter of George Little, farmer. The witnesses were John Potter and George Potter.<ref>[https://www.irishgenealogy.ie/files/civil/marriage_returns/marriages_1856/09507/5445820.pdf Cookstown civil marriage return, 15 April 1856, printed p.273, entry 43].</ref> The register gives Cookstown, without specifically naming Killycurragh as Benjamin’s residence.

Benjamin Glasgow, Esq., of Drapersfield provided a field for the Cookstown gathering on 12 July 1870, as reported three days later.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/387881589/ Belfast News-Letter, 15 July 1870, p.4].</ref> This current action follows the death dated 8 February 1870 above and strongly distinguishes the Drapersfield man from this Benjamin. The 1858 mill report’s uncle William and its ambiguous reference to Robert as father of the present plaintiff should therefore not be attached to this profile.<ref>[https://www.newspapers.com/image/390574459/ Belfast News-Letter, 22 July 1858, p.3].</ref>
